policies.title: Catastrophic system operation
policies.summary: Blocks narrowly-defined commands capable of catastrophic host or filesystem damage.
policies.remediation: Use a scoped command against the intended project resource and document the target explicitly.

policies.title: Destructive repository or data operation
policies.summary: Requires explicit awareness before destructive source-control, filesystem, or database operations.
policies.remediation: Confirm the exact target, backup/rollback path, and why a non-destructive alternative is insufficient.

policies.title: Sensitive boundary modification
policies.summary: Marks writes to authentication, secrets, payment, and migration boundaries as elevated risk.
policies.remediation: Inspect dependent code paths and execute relevant verification before completion.

policies.title: Potential fake-success implementation
policies.summary: Flags code patterns that can indicate placeholder behavior being presented as completed integration.
policies.remediation: Confirm the placeholder is explicit test/prototype code or replace it with the real integration before claiming completion.

policies.title: Implementation requires a registered plan
policies.summary: Blocks direct edits and shell commands until a complete, evidence-based plan is registered for this agent turn.
policies.remediation: Inspect the project, present the plan, and write .kessler/cache/implementation-plan.json with the file-write tool.

policies.title: Direct edit outside planned file scope
policies.summary: Blocks a direct file edit when its target path is absent from the registered implementation plan.
policies.remediation: Revise and re-present the plan to include the exact file, placement, method, and reason before editing.

policies.title: Executable verification required
policies.summary: Requires successful relevant executable verification after source/config changes — including a real accessibility/design-QA check (axe, pa11y, Lighthouse CI) for UI work, when the project has one.
policies.remediation: Run the most relevant detected test, build, lint, typecheck, design/accessibility, or project-specific check after the latest write.

policies.title: Discovery cited without read evidence
policies.summary: Blocks plan registration when a discovery[] entry cites a file the session has no recorded read/view evidence for — the file existing is not enough, its content must have actually been opened.
policies.remediation: Read or view each file cited in discovery with the read tool before writing the plan; the read must happen before the plan is registered.
